newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr, off day's lows.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr, off day's lows.

text.p: The Indian rupee rallied from early losses to end Thursday little changed from the opening levels, dealers said.
They said the rupee ended at 35.82/83 per dollar after touching day's low of 35.8625 in volatile trade. It opened at 35.81/83.
Dealers said a combination of corporate demand and short-covering by banks led to the rupee's fall after it had traded quietly in a 35.81 to 35.83 band for most of the morning.
"Besides demand from a large state-run bank, other banks and financial institutions were buying dollars today indicating good corporate demand," said a dealer.
"Besides, some banks were stuck with short dollar positions and their short-covering added to the dollar demand," he said.
Dealers said the rupee recovered as dollar supplies came into the market at 35.85 levels and demand eased.
The Reserve Bank of India bought dollars in small lots at 35.8275 rupees, a dealer said.
Forward premia moved up slightly on paying pressure, dealers said. The premia on six-month dollars ended Thursday at an annualised 8.1 percent against the previous close of 7.9.
